items.title: Clarence Ford Interview, 1975-12-10
items.q: But anyway, the Johnson Brothers, what broke that band was the Korean War, because players went to the service.

ctx.x: I heard that he was the brains behind.

He's one of the smartest, well one of the best musicians I know. Aside from financial things, I mean he's a national down-to-date musician. Because we were in a little Army Reserve band he was in also, where I learned a lot. This guy was a professor at Dillon and he had the band in charge and we'd go to camp twice a year, once a year, and we'd go to meetings twice a week. And he would show us things that he was teaching in college. And Harold Batiste was one of his students. And I saw Harold sit down and write…
Were the bands different up in Detroit?
